rounds.proof_sketch: Kernel launched with 1D block → blockDim.y=1 always. Mutated loop stride changes from blockDim.x (256) to blockDim.y (1), causing multiple threads to write same output locations. However, all threads compute identical values: mean/variance shared via reduction, input/gamma/beta arrays identical. Race condition is benign since all writes are identical values.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the Phase 3 loop stride from blockDim.x (256) to blockDim.y (1), creating overlapping writes across threads. However, since mean and variance are computed via shared memory reduction in Phases 1-2 (unchanged), all threads have identical values for mean, inv_std, and access the same input/gamma/beta arrays. Therefore, every thread computes the exact same normalized value for each output index. The race condition is benign because all racing writes store identical values. This structural property is independent of input values—no numerical input can cause threads to compute different values for the same output element.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. Would require launching kernel with 2D blocks where blockDim.y > 1, which requires modifying host code (not allowed). No value-level input can break the structural equivalence where all threads compute identical outputs.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should recognize benign race conditions where all threads write identical values. Such mutations require config-level changes (kernel launch parameters) to be killable, which should be flagged as a separate test category requiring infrastructure changes rather than value-level inputs.
